limitations: Ollama provides no authoritative prompt or output token IDs in this API; equal counts/text do not establish exact input identity.
vLLM prompt IDs/cache counters match all frozen workloads; output/numerical/quality correspondence is separate.
Ollama uses an explicitly recorded singleton-shape-only view; every tensor payload remains identical to source.
Native CPU console and external MLX GPU/API routes have different execution and latency boundaries.
Two 10-trial cohorts do not qualify tail latency or sustained behavior.
Memory is sampled with available lifetime counters, includes a reserve and can double-count shared pages; short-lived undiscovered work can be missed.
Native console and external HTTP observations were collected in separate serial campaigns, not one interleaved cross-engine campaign.
Reference baseline source revision is not recoverable from its frozen executable receipt; SHA/profile/compiler evidence is preserved without attributing the candidate checkout to it.
Installed external version metadata and eleven selected sources are checked; this is not a full-runtime source attestation.
First generated text is a nonempty client event, not first-content or first-visible latency. The native after-done flag is observed per cohort; it is false in both measured baseline cohorts.
External clock fields are scheduler request durations, not completed GPU operation timing.
The isolated finite-widening candidate is excluded from this report; its full performance retention is pending.
